notesStmt.note: Whitman was in the habit of ordering batches of specially printed poem slips, like this one, which he would sometimes sign or "correct" in small ways and present as mementos to friends and admirers. His signature here was almost certainly written sometime in late 1884 or January 1885
A proof slip of the poem "Of That Blithe Throat of Thine," which was first published in Harper's Monthly Magazine in January 1885. The poem was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: Of that Blithe Throat of Thine.

epigraph.p: [More than 83 degrees north—about a good days' steaming distance to the Pole by one of our fast oceaners in clear water—Greely heard the song of a single snow-bird merrily sounding over the desolation.]

lg.l: Of that blithe throat of thine from arctic bleak and blank,

I'll mind the lesson, solitary bird—let me too welcome chilling
drifts,

E'en the profoundest chill, as now—a torpid pulse, a brain un-
nerv'd,unnerv'd,
Old age land-lock'd within its winter bay—(cold, cold, O cold!)
These snowy hairs, my feeble arm, my frozen feet,
For them thy faith, thy rule I take, and grave it to the last;

Not summer's zones alone—not chants of youth, or south's warm
tides alone,
But held by sluggish floes, pack'd in the northern ice, the cumulus of years,
These with gay heart I also sing.
